title: Pull the hot dog past its hold time off a running roller grill with spring tongs and drop it in the discard pan
instruction: Use the tongs to take the tagged hot dog off the roller grill and drop it in the discard pan.
context: Most people have lifted food off something hot with tongs: a sausage off a home barbecue, a chop out of a grill pan, a serving of chips from a buffet tray, or a hot dog off the roller grill at a petrol station counter, where customers often take their own with the tongs provided. The same grip in each case: the tips close on round food that will not stay put (on a roller grill the "continually rotate" rollers keep turning it), and lift it straight up without dropping it or touching the hot food beside it. Here a 2.2 cm frank rests between two 25 mm rollers, its centre 3.7 mm above their tops, so 25 mm tips must close at its middle in the 4 mm above the rollers and lift it straight up. Closed high, it rolls out; pressed low, the tips jam on the rollers. Unlike stowing tongs, it is a pinch on round food that a moving surface keeps turning. Roller grills stand in well over two-thirds of US convenience stores (NACS).
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the counter, which is the station table. All parts true size. Roller grill: Avantco RG1830NS (sheet: 22 7/8 x 18 1/4 x 8 3/4 in, 58.1 x 46.4 x 22.2 cm; 11 non-stick rollers; 30 hot dogs; two heat zones), stainless, standing on its feet, front edge at x 26, back at x 72.4, from y -18 to y 40.1, its end housings 22.2 cm tall. Rollers: 11 along y, each 49.6 cm long (y -14.8 to 34.8), 25 mm across on a 3.4 cm pitch, the front axis at x 29, tops 19 cm up (diameter, pitch, height and speed are estimates, since the sheet gives none: ranges 25 to 28 mm, 3.2 to 3.5 cm, 17 to 21 cm, 2 to 6 rpm; across them a frank's centre stays 3 mm or more above the roller tops). All turn the same way at 3 rpm, their tops moving toward the back, as the maker says they "continually rotate". Grooves are numbered 1 (front) to 10; groove 2 is centred at x 34.1. Franks: 12 standard beef franks, 8 to the pound (57 g), 15 cm long and 2.2 cm across, in grooves 2, 4, 6 and 8, three to a groove at y -7, 9.5 and 26 (1.5 cm end gaps); grooves 1, 3, 5 and 7 are empty, so the tagged frank has an empty groove on each side. The tagged frank, past its hold time, is the darker one in groove 2 at y -7, marked by a red polypropylene clip tag, 50 x 38 mm, on the front rail in line with it. Tongs: 9 in (22.9 cm) stainless utility tongs, 110 g, two 20 mm wide arms on a sprung hinge with a pull ring, tips 25 mm wide with round ends, opening to 7 cm; spring about 4 N at the tips held 5 cm apart and 8 N closed on a frank (estimate). They lie on their arms' edges on a folded cotton bar towel (30 x 10 x 1 cm, x 27 to 57, y -51 to -41), the hinge at (53, -46), tips toward the robot. So the towel and tongs lie on the counter just right of the discard pan, on its side away from the grill; in the setup view the right arm, at its ready pose, hangs over them and hides them. Discard pan: a 1/3-size stainless steam-table pan, 12 3/4 x 6 7/8 x 4 in (32.4 x 17.5 x 10.2 cm), 0.5 kg, centred at (44, -30), long side along x, beside the grill's right end. Frictions (estimates): frank on roller 0.5, on tong tips about 0.7, on pan steel 0.4. Both arms start at their ready pose, grippers open. Reset (about 2 min): discard the frank in the pan (or wipe the dowel), lay a fresh one in groove 2 at y -7 by a tape mark on the front rail, return any moved frank to its rail mark, lay the tongs on the towel, hinge on its tape mark, and send the arms to ready. Run limit 90 s (1,800 steps). Real trial (about US$355): the RG1830NS (about $330), 9 in utility tongs ($5), a 1/3-size pan ($10), a bar towel ($3), and for each trial a fresh standard frank from the refrigerator (4 C), handled with gloves and discarded after, or a 2.2 cm hardwood dowel 15 cm long, sanded, finished with food-grade mineral oil and weighted to 57 g. Before the trials, measure the roller diameter and pitch with a caliper, the roller speed by timing 10 turns of a taped roller, and the tongs' spring with a luggage scale at the tips. Run the grill switched on with both heat zones at off, so the rollers turn cold; check that they turn before the first trial. If a unit turns its rollers only with heat on, set the front zone to its lowest, use the dowel, and fit heat-resistant silicone finger sleeves (about $8) over the gripper pads; the gripper touches only the tongs' hinge half, well away from the rollers. Film one 60 fps phone video from the front-right, at rail height, about 60 cm away, framing the right half of the grill, the pan and the towel: it sees the tips close, the lift against the 3.4 cm roller pitch, the pan, the towel and the last 1 s.
scoring: Terms. Tongs picked up: a fingertip within 15 mm of them and they are 5 cm or more above where they lay (real: the video). Closed on: both tong tips in contact with the tagged frank, squeezing it, on opposite sides of its axis, one frank diameter apart (sim: each tip within 1 mm of its surface, the two contacts at least 154 degrees apart round the axis; real trial: the video shows both tips on its sides), and no gripper finger within 6 mm of the frank at any time it counts as carried. A frank held by the gripper, or lying across the tips' edges in a cradle, is not closed on. Lifted: the frank's centre 4 cm or more above where it lay (real: the video, against the 3.4 cm roller pitch). Carried: it was lifted in the closed tips and held in them until it was over the pan, the tips never off it for more than 0.5 s (a regrip is free; a frank set down and left, then pushed, is not carried). In the pan: its centre over the pan's floor and below the rim, no part of the tongs (arms, hinge, ring or tips) within 5 mm of it, moving slower than 5 mm/s (real: a photo into the pan, no tong touching). Three tiers, from the state now: 0.33, the tongs picked up; 0.67, the tongs closed on the tagged frank and it is lifted (or it was carried to the pan and lies in it, whether or not a tong still touches it); 1.0, the frank was carried to the pan and lies in it, no tong touching it and still, held for 1 s. One failure voids the run (score 0): the tagged frank dropped, falling 3 cm or more anywhere but into the pan. Free: regrips, retries, time, the other franks, rollers and the tongs afterwards. So a frank pushed, scooped or batted into the pan, or set back on the grill and pushed in, never earns the last two tiers. Possible scores: 0, 0.33, 0.67, 1.0.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, 240 Hz, GPU; franks rigid capsules; rollers driven at 3 rpm, no heat. Tong arms 2.5 mm thick (real 1 mm), not colliding: a joint stop stands for the tips meeting; spring 8 N m/rad (estimate); flat tips; rigid towel. Limits: carry is read from tip contacts, not force, so a frank lifted, set back and pinched again, or dragged pinched into the pan, counts as carried; a cradle on the tips' edges and a two-hand carry were tried once each and scored low, not proven shut.
